Naturalism is the broader thesis that the natural world and scientific methods are the proper basis for understanding everything, including human affairs, without appeal to the supernatural. Positivism is a narrower doctrine that only empirically verifiable claims count as knowledge and that metaphysics is meaningless, so it is best seen as one strict form of naturalism. Neither option in the team note describes this distinction, and both seem to concern international relations theory rather than these philosophical positions.
